verses.1: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to Jehovah. They said, “We will sing to Jehovah, for he is great and glorious; his horse is swift, and his rider is exalted in heaven.”
verses.2: May Aziz and Zimrat Yah be with me, and may they bring me salvation. They are my gods, and they will help me.
verses.3: Yehova, a man of war. Yehova, his name.
verses.4: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army shot their arrows into the sea. And from among his six hundred men, only a few survived in the sea.
verses.5: The clouds covered the sky, like a blanket.
verses.6: May Your Name be praised, O LORD! May You save me from this weakness. May Your Name be praised, O LORD! May You comfort me.
verses.7: And in your abundance of pride, you will be destroyed. Your children will be sent away to eat like garbage.
verses.8: And in your wings, waters were gathered together; they stood like dead bodies. The mountains became silent in the heart of the sea.
verses.9: O Jehovah, I say: “I will fill my soul with your gifts. May your kingdom be filled with peace and joy.”
verses.10: You flew through the skies like a bird that glided over the vast seas.
verses.11: Who is like Jehovah in His holiness? Who can be as mighty as He in the sacred place where He creates songs of praise?
verses.12: Your right hand will swallow him up; the earth will devour him.
verses.13: I have rested in your mercy; you have redeemed this people. You have brought them into your holy place by your power.
verses.14: Hear, nations! The army of Ahaz, the rulers of Philistia, are angry.
verses.15: Then the ears of Adam were frightened. The sheep and cattle trembled with fear. All the inhabitants of Kenaan were terrified.
verses.16: Fear and terror will be upon them because of your great power. Their suffering will be like that of a leaf that is torn apart by the wind. But your people will survive, O LORD, until that time comes.
verses.17: May it be established and fixed on your mountain of inheritance. May Jehovah act through you from His holy temple. May your hands be able to create.
verses.18: Yehova shall reign forever and ever.
verses.19: For a horse of Pharaoh came forth, with its rider and his retinue. Jehovah made the waters rise above them. And the children of Israel walked on dry ground, within the midst of the sea.
verses.20: And Mary, the prophetess, took the rod in her hand. Then all the women followed her, carrying torches and weapons.
verses.21: And Marya sang songs to Jehovah, saying that the horse was mighty and its rider was high above the clouds.
verses.22: And Moses led Israel out of the sea. They went towards the shore of the Red Sea. They walked on the shore for three days, but they couldn’t find any water.
verses.23: And they came to Marah. They couldn’t drink water from Marah, because it was bitter. That’s why it was named Marah.
verses.24: And the people cried out to Moses, saying, “What shall we do?”
verses.25: And he cried out to Jehovah. Jehovah sent a tree to kill him, and he was thrown into the water. There, he died. But there, he received laws and judgments.
verses.26: And he said, “If you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and if you obey His commands, and if you keep all His laws, then I, the LORD, will heal you. I will not punish you, for I am the LORD your healer.”
verses.27: And they came to Eilma. There were there twenty-two eyes of water, and seventy palms. They stopped there on the water.
